correctness.rationale: In the three-oscillator sine-coupled triangle, node 3 gives b sinφ=sinψ, and injection node 1 gives P=sin(φ+ψ)+b sinφ, with φ,ψ≥0 in the strict security sector. For δ=φ+ψ, the unique principal solution is φ=atan(sinδ/(b+cosδ)); ψ=δ-φ. Differentiating the sine balance shows dφ/dδ,dψ/dδ>0; dP/dδ=cosδ+b cosφ dφ/dδ>0 for δ≤γ<π/2. The first active cap is δ=γ when b≤sinη/sin(γ-η), otherwise ψ=η. Substitution gives the two exact capacity formulas, continuity, strict increase then decrease and peak sinγ+sinη. The exact min-endpoint robust criterion follows unimodality. Every secure equilibrium has positive weighted cosine conductances, giving two strictly negative transverse Jacobian eigenvalues; a separate principal branch below π/2 shows stable locking beyond the tighter security bound at sufficiently large b. Independently checked phase balances and formula values for b=0.1,0.5,1,2,10 with γ=π/3, η=π/6; these samples corroborate only.
